what-is-lockin.question: What is Lockin?
what-is-lockin.shortAnswer: Lockin is a connected study environment that brings sheets, questions, notes and review together in one experience. It currently serves medicine and dentistry students in Libya.

who-is-lockin-for.question: Who is Lockin available for?
who-is-lockin-for.shortAnswer: Medicine students in Tripoli, and First and Second Year dentistry students in Tripoli, Benghazi and Zawiya. The subjects and questions each student sees depend on their study path and the content published for it.

supported-universities.question: Does Lockin cover every university and year?
supported-universities.shortAnswer: Not yet. The study paths you can choose now are dentistry (First and Second Year) in Tripoli, Benghazi and Zawiya, and medicine in Tripoli (Batch 60 and 61). Published content differs between paths, and other universities and years are not supported yet.

need-account.question: Do I need an account to study?
need-account.shortAnswer: Yes. The introduction pages and the help center are public, while study materials, progress and notes live inside your account and follow its access.

open-materials.question: How do I reach my sheets?
open-materials.shortAnswer: Start from Materials in your account, then choose the subject and an available sheet.
detailedSteps: Open Materials after signing in.
Choose a subject shown for your study path.
Open the sheet, then an available edition of it, to reach the study workspace.

cohort-content.question: Why are my subjects different from a classmate’s?
cohort-content.shortAnswer: Your subject list depends on the study path and the year or cohort registered on your account, and on the published content. A different path can mean different subjects and questions. In Second Year Dentistry, a student may also add up to two First Year subjects, which then appear for them only.

sheet-editions.question: What is the difference between the sheet editions shown?
sheet-editions.shortAnswer: A sheet may show a University edition and a Lockin edition when both are available. Only published editions that can be opened appear; not every sheet has both.

about-settings.question: Where do I find information about Lockin inside the app?
about-settings.shortAnswer: Open Settings, then «About Lockin» for the introduction and features, or «Support» for the help center and its guides.

open-pdf.question: How do I open a sheet to read it?
open-pdf.shortAnswer: Choose a subject, then a sheet and an available edition. Open the study workspace and use Normal Study for reading and notes.
detailedSteps: Open Materials and choose the subject.
Open the sheet and an available edition.
Choose Normal Study if a study mode chooser appears.

pdf-notes.question: Can I write notes on the PDF?
pdf-notes.shortAnswer: Yes. The sheet’s study workspace has pen, highlighter and text tools. Your notes belong to your account’s workspace.

pen-tool.question: How do I write on the sheet’s pages?
pen-tool.shortAnswer: Open the sheet in the study workspace, choose the pen from the toolbar, then write or draw on the page.
detailedSteps: Open the sheet’s study workspace.
Choose the pen and adjust its color or thickness if needed.
Write on the page and check the save status before leaving the session.

highlight-tool.question: How do I highlight the important parts?
highlight-tool.shortAnswer: Use the highlighter in the study workspace to mark important places on the page. Highlights are part of your workspace notes, not an edit to the original file.

erase-marks.question: How do I erase what I wrote?
erase-marks.shortAnswer: Choose the eraser to remove marks you made in the workspace. The eraser never removes the original PDF text.

text-notes.question: Can I add typed text?
text-notes.shortAnswer: Yes. A text tool sits next to the drawing tools in the study workspace, for typed notes close to the page you are reviewing.

notes-private.question: Can other students see my notes?
notes-private.shortAnswer: Your own notes belong to your account and the document. If you choose to share a copy of your PDF marks, students with access to that sheet can see it. Marks you don’t share stay private, and the public pages never show your notes, answers or files.

pdf-original.question: Does writing change the original sheet?
pdf-original.shortAnswer: Marks and notes are saved in the workspace linked to the sheet. Using them does not edit the content of the original published file.

active-study-what.question: What is Active Study?
active-study-what.shortAnswer: A study mode that splits the sheet into parts, with a short test after each part and a final test at the end. On new prepared sheets you can choose the pages and questions per test, or use the Pomodoro style: a focus timer, then a test on the pages you read. The standard style stays available.

start-active-study.question: How do I start Active Study?
start-active-study.shortAnswer: Open the sheet’s workspace, choose Active Study and a difficulty, then press «Start Active Study» when the option is available.
detailedSteps: Open the subject, the sheet and an available edition.
Choose Active Study and a difficulty.
If «Customize» appears, set the pages per test (up to 10) and the number of questions (up to 30), or choose «Use standard style».
If Pomodoro style appears in the Focus reader, choose the timer length: 25, 45 or 50 minutes of focus. When the timer ends, choose up to 40 questions on the pages you read, then take a break.
Press «Start Active Study». If questions aren’t available, choose Normal Study or another prepared sheet.

active-availability.question: Is Active Study available for every sheet?
active-availability.shortAnswer: No. It needs the sheet and suitable questions for the chosen difficulty to be prepared. Having a PDF alone does not make a sheet ready for Active Study.

active-difficulty.question: Can I choose the difficulty of Active Study?
active-difficulty.shortAnswer: Yes. Choose easy, medium or hard. On new prepared sheets you can customize up to 10 pages and 30 questions per test, or choose the Pomodoro style, which tests the pages you read once the focus timer ends with up to 40 questions, depending on what’s available. Progress is kept separately for each style.

active-parts.question: What happens after I read the sheet’s pages?
active-parts.shortAnswer: After reading the available pages, open the part’s test. Passing it unlocks the next pages, and earlier pages stay readable. The test is tied to the pages set for that study session.
detailedSteps: In the standard or custom style, keep reading to the last page of the part to unlock its test.
In the Pomodoro style, a screen for choosing the number of questions appears when the focus timer ends, and the test is fixed to the new pages you reached in that session.

Questions are spread as evenly as possible across the pages. One page provides up to 15 questions and the Pomodoro limit is 40 in total; if there are fewer questions than pages, pages spread across the range are chosen.

active-final.question: Is there a test at the end of Active Study?
active-final.shortAnswer: Yes. After the parts there is a final test that brings together what you studied. Its number of questions depends on the sheet’s setup, not one number for every subject.

active-resume.question: How do I return to an earlier Active Study session?
active-resume.shortAnswer: Use exit with save, then open the same sheet with the same difficulty and style to resume. Custom session settings stay saved, and offline results only count once the server confirms them.

active-restart.question: What happens if I restart Active Study from the beginning?
active-restart.shortAnswer: After you confirm, restarting returns the session for the chosen difficulty and style to the first pages. Changing the settings of a custom session you started asks you to confirm a new session; the earlier session stays in the archive and your PDF notes are unaffected.

normal-or-active.question: What is the difference between Normal Study and Active Study?
normal-or-active.shortAnswer: Normal Study is for reading and working on the sheet; Active Study adds parts, questions and a final test on prepared sheets. The PDF tools stay part of the study workspace.

pomodoro-study.question: How do I study with the Pomodoro technique in Lockin?
pomodoro-study.shortAnswer: Choose Pomodoro style in Active Study inside the Focus reader. You read with a focus timer, test yourself on the pages you reached when it ends, then take a break. Every four tests earn a long break.
detailedSteps: Open a new prepared sheet in the Focus reader and choose Active Study and a difficulty.
Choose Pomodoro style, then the timer length: 25 minutes of focus and 5 of break, 45 and 10, or 50 and 10.
Read until the timer ends, then choose the number of questions (up to 40) to test the pages you read in that session.
Review your result page by page, and tap any weak page to read it again.
After every four page tests you get a long break, and the final test brings together everything you studied.

custom-active-study.question: How do I set the number of pages and questions in Active Study?
custom-active-study.shortAnswer: On new prepared sheets, press «Customize» before you start, then set up to 10 pages per test and up to 30 questions. The final test stays the same, and you can go back to the standard style at any time.
detailedSteps: Open the sheet and choose Active Study and a difficulty.
Press «Customize» if it appears, and set the pages per test and the questions.
The highest number of questions depends on the pages in the shortest part, because each page provides up to 15 questions.
Changing the settings of a custom session you started opens a new session after you confirm, and the earlier session’s progress is kept in the archive.

question-sources.question: Where do I find the questions?
question-sources.shortAnswer: Open Questions in your account, then the source and subject available for your study path. Published questions differ by subject and study path.
detailedSteps: Open Questions.
Choose an available source, then the subject.
Choose a published question set and start the test using the options shown.

practical-questions.question: Does Lockin support practical dentistry questions?
practical-questions.shortAnswer: Some practice sources include questions based on slides and images, or on locating a spot. Their availability depends on the subject and published content; they don’t necessarily cover every subject or every student.

mixed-questions.question: Why can’t I open Mix?
mixed-questions.shortAnswer: The Mix source isn’t available right now. Use one of the question sources available for your study path in Questions.

question-explanations.question: Are there explanations for the answers?
question-explanations.shortAnswer: An answer explanation appears on the question and review screens when one is available. Not every question has a published explanation.

find-mistakes.question: How do I review my mistakes?
find-mistakes.shortAnswer: Open the Review Center, then the review bank or «Start review» when there are active questions. Mistakes from supported sources are the ones that enter this system.
detailedSteps: Open the Review Center.
Choose «Open Review Bank» or «Start review» if it appears.
Choose the subject, answer the questions shown, then check your review result.

saved-mistakes.question: Is every wrong answer saved in the review bank?
saved-mistakes.shortAnswer: Your mistakes in questions that support review are saved. Mistakes from other activity, or attempts that never reached the server, don’t enter the review bank.

repeat-mistake.question: What happens if I get the same question wrong again?
repeat-mistake.shortAnswer: The review bank keeps the question and a record of the repeated mistake, instead of treating it as a new question each time, so you can return to the point that needs attention.

mastered-question.question: Where does a question go after I answer it correctly in review?
mastered-question.shortAnswer: It leaves the active review list and becomes eligible for later recall under the review policy. Leaving the active list does not delete its record.

empty-review.question: What does an empty review bank mean?
empty-review.shortAnswer: There are no active questions that need review right now. The record of mastered questions may still be kept, and it doesn’t mean your data was lost.

weekly-recall.question: What is Weekly Recall?
weekly-recall.shortAnswer: A periodic memory test using eligible questions you have already corrected in the review bank. It appears when suitable questions are available for your account.

weekly-not-ready.question: Why does Weekly Recall show as not ready?
weekly-not-ready.shortAnswer: There may be no eligible mastered questions yet. Start by correcting questions in the review bank; the system won’t create an empty test just because a week has passed.

start-weekly.question: How do I start the memory test?
start-weekly.shortAnswer: From the Review Center, use the button to start or continue the memory test when it appears. If it isn’t available, work through the review bank first.

weekly-errors.question: What happens to mistakes in the memory test?
weekly-errors.shortAnswer: Questions you answer wrongly in Weekly Recall return to the active review bank, based on the test result.

progress-page.question: How do I follow my progress?
progress-page.shortAnswer: Open Progress to see your recorded activity, progress points and their history, and your streak days. These are usage indicators, not a guarantee of an exam grade or an academic comparison.

periodic-reports.question: Where do I find my weekly summary?
periodic-reports.shortAnswer: When your weekly summary is ready, the app shows «Your summary for the week is ready»; press «Open» to read it. A summary may not appear without enough activity.

private-and-public.question: What appears in search and what stays private?
private-and-public.shortAnswer: Only the introduction, feature and guide pages are public. Study materials, account data, notes and answers stay behind the app’s access controls and are not in the public sitemap.

account-security.question: How do I protect my account data?
account-security.shortAnswer: Don’t share your password, verification codes or recovery links with anyone. Use your own account to reach the study data linked to it.

supported-access.question: Does the introduction page give me access to every sheet?
supported-access.shortAnswer: No. The page only explains how Lockin works. Access to a sheet or questions depends on your study path, the published content and your account or subscription access.

first-year-subjects.question: Can I add First Year subjects as a Second Year dentistry student?
first-year-subjects.shortAnswer: Yes. Second Year Dentistry students can add up to two First Year subjects they are studying this year, from the «Add a First Year subject» button in Materials.
detailedSteps: Open Materials in your account.
Press «Add a First Year subject», choose the subject and confirm.
The choice is final. To replace a subject later, open Settings, then «My subjects», and send a request for an administrator to review.

missing-materials.question: Why is a subject or sheet missing?
missing-materials.shortAnswer: Your study path may not be supported or have published content yet, or the sheet may not be openable. Check the study path on your account, and don’t change it just to try: changing it can affect your progress.

missing-questions.question: Why do I see a message that there are no questions?
missing-questions.shortAnswer: Publishing a sheet and publishing its questions are separate. A file can be available for reading before questions are available for the chosen subject or source.

reader-unavailable.question: What should I do if a sheet won’t open?
reader-unavailable.shortAnswer: Check your connection, that the sheet is available and your account’s access, then use retry if it appears. If the problem continues, describe it from Settings without sharing a protected file or sensitive account details.

notes-not-synced.question: What should I do if my notes didn’t sync?
notes-not-synced.shortAnswer: Wait for the save or sync status shown and check your connection. Don’t clear browser data or sign out as a first step before you are sure your work is saved.

active-start-error.question: What should I do if Active Study won’t start?
active-start-error.shortAnswer: Check that the sheet and difficulty are ready and your connection, and use retry if it appears. You can continue with Normal Study when it’s available; we don’t assume the sheet’s questions are ready.

contact-support.question: How do I reach support?
contact-support.shortAnswer: Open Settings, then «Support», for the help center. To report a problem from your account, use «Suggest» in Settings, choose the problem category and send a short description.
detailedSteps: Open Settings, then Support.
Look through the guides that fit the problem.
To report it, open «Suggest» and write what happened and what you were trying to do, without your password or verification code.
